• Ministry of Justice (MOJ) have produced a five- year National strategy, under which a comprehensive institutional and legal reform action plan is agreed upon to enable and facilitate the ministry’s critical role in realizing the democratic transition in Sudan, with due respect to principles of inclusion, transparency, accessibility, and respect for human rights. This was • developed by the conference of judges (awaiting validation) who identified the areas of reform and means of implementation. • MOJ also finalized Three draft legislations with the support of UNDP, for the formation the Human Right Commission, Constitution-Making Process and Commission and Election Commission • A baseline study assessing Sudan legal System, conducted by a national expert in support of MOJ, was produced. Some of the findings include…. • Three laws passed by the government for the establishment of the three commissions named by the Constitutional Document and Juba Peace Agreement as top priorities, to lead the transitional agenda on peace and security, accountability, and transparency, namely the Peace Commission, Transitional Justice Commission and Anti-corruption Commission. • Recommendations of the judiciary conference were produced, however the process of darting the strategic plan was hampered by the political situation resulted from the military coup de etate that took place in 25 October 2021. • The support has also been extended to the Attorney General Office and the Bar Association with the view to developing their strategies for reform. Also, in support of peace building, transitional justice, human rights protection, and stabilization of the transition, the CO supported MOJ in conducting a wide consultation around the draft legislations setting the Peace Commission, Human Rights Commission, Transitional Justice Commission and Anticorruption Commission. • in support of peace building, transitional justice, human rights protection, and stabilization of the transition, MOJ was supported in conducting a wide consultation around the draft legislations setting the Peace Commission, Human Rights Commission, Transitional Justice Commission and Anticorruption Commission. These efforts will be continued in 2022 as a result of, an increase of the number of cases handled by justice institutions, paralegals and traditional mechanisms has been increased excessively • The political situation in Sudan was in jeopardy even during the transitional period, these massive conflicts entered into its peaks when the military takeover on the 25th of October 2021 remains the chief challenge, as most of our portfolio interventions have been put on hold. Also, we three strategic conferences with the AGO on ‘AG National Strategy’, MOJ on ‘Human Rights Situation in Sudan, the transition and beyond’, and Bar Association on ‘Reform of the Legal Profession’, were cancelled. These conferences were expected to feed into the reform agenda of the justice sector. The impact of the coup has led to suspension of planned electoral and constitutional process consultations and hate speech and anti-racial roundtable discussion. • With the support of FWs, the CO supported the government on developing a five-year National Strategy for judicial reform|0|1As a strong and continuous efforts and supports received from FWs, UNDP managed to swiftly implement the targeted thematic areas in 2021|0|0|1The project workshops and seminars to support the transitional period in Sudan were widely covered by UNDP media channels (website, twitter, etc) along with wide local media coverage
